docs.title: NLP Esperantilo
docs.text:
Welcome to NLP Esperantilo, a project made of two complementary parts:

  • A Python library for rule-based Natural Language Processing in Esperanto.
  • This documentation, a guide and tutorial to build that library and its surrounding tooling from scratch.

Work in progress

This site is the scaffold of the documentation. Every section already has its structure and its planned contents, but the contents themselves are still being written.

docs.title: Who is this for
docs.text: This guide is aimed at university students who have to build their own Esperanto NLP library. Readers are expected to have some technical background, but not necessarily experience with the specific tools and topics explained here.

docs.title: What this guide covers
docs.text: Section Contents Git Version control: how Git works, its most used commands and how to undo changes. GitHub Collaborative workflow, pull requests, GitHub Actions, repository protection and GitHub Pages. Python Library Packaging, project layout, API design, installation and testing. Esperanto History, grammar, vocabulary and resources — the linguistic rules the library encodes.

docs.title: What this guide does not cover
docs.text:
Two topics are deliberately left out, because they are taught in the course lectures:

  • Web scraping and API consumption (requests, beautifulsoup4, the Wikipedia API, and similar).
  • Text-mining and Machine-Learning classification (feature extraction, vectorization, model training and evaluation, metrics).

The focus here is the software-engineering tooling needed to work like a professional team, and the Esperanto domain knowledge needed to write a rule-based NLP library.

docs.title: Reading the documentation
docs.text: The guide can be read from start to finish, but the four sections are mostly independent. A reader who already knows Git and GitHub can jump straight to Python Library or Esperanto.

docs.title: Building the documentation locally
docs.text:
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

The site is then available at http://127.0.0.1:8000. Every push to main rebuilds it and publishes it to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: What GitHub Pages is
docs.text: Free static hosting served directly from a repository, and the URL it produces: https://<user>.github.io/<repository>/.

docs.title: Enabling it
docs.text: In Settings → Pages, set the source to Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root). The workflows create and update that branch; nothing has to be committed there by hand.

docs.title: How this site is deployed
docs.text:
Two workflows write to the same gh-pages branch, to different places:

Workflow Trigger Publishes to Visible at docs.yml push to main branch root the public site docs-preview.yml pull request pr-preview/pr-<number>/ the preview URL posted on the pull request 
flowchart LR
    PR[Pull request] --> BP[mkdocs build --strict]
    BP --> PV["gh-pages:/pr-preview/pr-N/"]
    PV --> C[Comment with the preview URL]
    M[Push to main] --> BM[mkdocs build --strict]
    BM --> RT["gh-pages:/ (root)"]
    RT --> S[Public site]

docs.title: Previewing a pull request
docs.text:
Every pull request gets its own copy of the whole site, built from the branch under review, at:

https://jparisu.github.io/nlp-esperantilo/pr-preview/pr-<number>/

A bot comment on the pull request links to it, and the link updates on every push. The preview is deleted when the pull request is merged or closed.

Two details make this work without ever touching the public site:

  • the production deployment runs with clean-exclude: pr-preview/, so publishing the real site does not delete the previews;
  • the preview build overrides site_url, so canonical links and the language switcher stay inside the preview.

Nothing reaches the front page until the pull request is merged — that is what makes a preview safe to hand to a reviewer.

Pull requests from forks

A fork's pull request runs with a read-only token and cannot publish. Its documentation is still built and checked, it just gets no preview URL.

docs.title: Publishing your own
docs.text: The steps to reproduce this setup in another repository: enable Pages on a gh-pages branch, allow workflows to write to the repository (Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions), and copy the two workflows.

docs.title: A spaCy-like API
docs.text:
spaCy is the reference model for this project. This subsection shows, with short examples, what a good NLP interface looks like:

  • typed objects such as Doc and Token,
  • typed function signatures with type hints,
  • illustrative snippets,
  • links to the spaCy API documentation.

The goal is a concrete target to imitate when designing the Doc / Token interface of the Esperanto library.

docs.title: NLP Esperantilo
docs.text:
Bonvenon al NLP Esperantilo, projekto konsistanta el du partoj:

  • Python-biblioteko por regul-bazita komputila lingvistiko en Esperanto.
  • Ĉi tiu dokumentaro, gvidilo por konstrui tiun bibliotekon kaj ĝiajn ilojn de nulo.

Laboro en progreso

Ĉi tiu paĝaro estas la skeleto de la dokumentaro. Ĉiu sekcio jam havas sian strukturon, sed la enhavo ankoraŭ estas verkata. La paĝoj sen Esperanta traduko montriĝas en la angla.

docs.title: Sekcioj
docs.text: Sekcio Enhavo Git Versikontrolo: kiel Git funkcias kaj ĝiaj plej uzataj komandoj. GitHub Kunlabora fluo, kunfandaj petoj, GitHub Actions kaj GitHub Pages. Python-Biblioteko Pakado, strukturo, API-dezajno, instalado kaj testado. Esperanto Historio, gramatiko, vortprovizo kaj lernorimedoj.
